current_bottleneck: The distributed matcher previously deleted every party-local MPC output and reopened the original encrypted order share in the next round, while the settlement process maintained the only mutable private-book state.
causal_hypothesis: Persisting each party's post-match Shamir evaluations, binding them to the execution receipt and advancing their public pointers only after canonical DeFMI finality will let the next round consume the exact Maker remainder without a coordinator-held private book.
single_intended_change: Add a fixed private-book Persistence ABI, durable owner-only node storage, signed parent and output digests, canonical-finality-gated head advancement, and Maker-to-Taker carry-forward in the integrated seven-node acceptance path.

baseline.limitation: The central settlement process held the mutable clear private book; MP-SPDZ party state was deleted after each round.

most_likely_prediction_error: MP-SPDZ Persistence output may use a runtime directory or wire representation different from the parser assumptions, causing the node to reject its own state file before Maker finality can be recorded.
rejection_rules: any party fails to write exactly 36 private-book state shares
any private-state or parent digest is zero
two node-local private-state files have the same digest
Maker heads advance before canonical reservation finality
Taker execution does not bind the finalized Maker head
trade price is not 100 or quantity is not 40
Taker DvP does not reach canonical finality
validator roots diverge or restart recovery fails
the public artifact exposes order fields, local file paths or Shamir shares
the artifact claims collaborative zkPI, account-free notes, independent operators, WAN or HSM evidence
promotion_rules: the complete Maker reserve, private-head finalization, Taker match, DvP, second private-head finalization and validator-restart path succeeds
the artifact records the exact contract SHA-256 and this manifest identifier
remote formatting, Clippy and workspace tests remain green
the observed result is recorded once in the append-only experiment ledger
